steps.text: There! My room's right there!
Faster, for heaven's sake!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: The Catastrophe is near, sir. Please make haste.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Don't rush me! I know where my art supplies are. We can go as soon as I grab them!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They're right under the shelf...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They're gone!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They were right here! Where did they go?!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: How much of a hurry were they in?! They knocked my things over!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They ruined a great work of art! Criminals!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Calm down. Does anyone else live here?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The landlady... Frau Perry. A housewife who knows nothing of art. She couldn't tell the sunset from an egg in the frypan.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Check the list to see if they have been evacuated.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I hardly ever spoke to her. Do I even have her contact information?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Mr. Devlin, you just got a new message on your communicator. Here.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: 'Herr Devlin, since you were away, I packed your things into a suitcase at the door, so you can take them and evacuate as soon as you return.'

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: 'Be safe. —Perry'

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Thank goodness! What a saint!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Is that everything then? I'll place them in the truck.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Yes. Let's go.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Thank goodness, I can paint on the way.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Give me some room to paint!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Sir, try not to sit like that. You could fall off.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Oh no! My brushes! My paints!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I knew I shouldn't have trusted that stupid woman!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The canvas is ruined! The brushes have been soaked in paint! All the paint is mixed up! It's all useless now!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: It's just a painting. You'll get another chance.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: No... there will never be another chance!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I've chased Catastrophes for so long, all for the moment when I could capture one's majesty with my own canvas and brush...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Sir...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: My painting, my dream, my life, everything... gone.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Leave me alone!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Didn't you hear me? I said to leave me alone!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What time do you think it is?! The sun's already setting!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I don't need counselling! I'm not dead! Piss off!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: This is my last warning. Knock one more time, and I'll—

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Oh... it's you.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Good evening, Mr. Devlin.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Er, good evening... You were the one who forecasted the Catastrophe... Er... something-Island?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Rhodes Island. I'm an operator from Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Oh, er, that's it?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I introduced myself when we first we met. Don't tell me you've forgotten my name, after we've spent this entire trip together?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: O-Of course not. You're... you're...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Tsukinogi!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I'm glad I made an impression on you after all.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Anyway, I have a few questions for you. I apologize if I'm interrupting anything.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Are you feeling any better?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Thanks to you folks. Not that I was injured to begin with.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Good to hear. What about in terms of mental health? Anything we can help you with?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Well, my painting's done for. Couldn't get any worse on that end.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I see. Are you having any difficulties living at the accommodation site? You seem to have declined all visitors.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Difficulties... If I had to say, it would be great if my 'friendly' neighbors stopped bothering me.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I'm not registering for anything, I'm not interested in any 'Post-Catastrophe Mutual Aid Group', I don't want to see anybody's long faces, and I especially don't want to be made to answer pointless questions at my own door.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Is that all then?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I'm not here to make you uncomfortable. If you want me to stop, just say so.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Don't you Catastrophe Messengers leave as soon as the Catastrophe's over? Why are you still here?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Have you ever met any others?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Er... no, only read about them in books.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: There are many kinds of Catastrophe Messengers. Some take an interest in things other than their jobs. Others simply quit.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: As for me, I have my reasons for staying. For example, I've taken an interest in your situation.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Spare me. There are plenty of others who'd prefer your attention. I hear crying outside every night.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: That was simply one of many reasons. Maybe it's the scenery that keeps me here.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: There are plenty of sights worth seeing; for example, a hill with beautiful sunsets.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Perhaps that might interest a disciple of the great Leithanian landscape artist Leon... a prodigy who devoted his life to the pursuit of light and shadow.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: You looked into my background?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: What art lover wouldn't know a thing or two about the greats?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: The landscape that you left behind before you left Leithanien... The refined touches capturing the moment when the sunset fades away... It was most impressive.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Rubbish. It couldn't compare to the beauty of a Catastrophe. Nothing could.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Painting aside, seeing beautiful sights can still help soothe one's mind. If you're interested—

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I'm not. I won't be going.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I appreciate that you and your colleagues helped me escape the Catastrophe, but that doesn't change the fact that my painting was ruined.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: If you were just a little quicker, a little more decisive in driving away those rioters...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Maybe I could have made it back and saved my supplies before Frau Perry 'packed' them for me.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: So I don't need your concern. Do whatever you want, just don't bother me.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I sincerely hope this is the last time I see you, Ms. Tsukinogi.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Regardless, it was a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Devlin.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Incidentally, I do have a little gift for you before I leave.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: This isn't part of the job, just a token from one art lover to another. I hope you can accept it.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I'll leave it here then. I wish you a good evening.
There is no color on the blank canvas, only shadows.
He gazes at their swaying edges.
There, light and shadow break apart like the void.
He lashes out, knocking over the easel.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I can't paint...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Damn it, I can't paint!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The Catastrophe's magnificent, beautiful song of light and shadow, that ensemble of colors... it will never come again.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What is there to paint if I can't even pick up my brush?!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Her gift...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Art supplies, paint... clearly meant as compensation.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: How did she even know that I used this brand of paint? I never mentioned it in interviews... Did she deduce it from the paintings?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Nothing of value though... I shouldn't have expected much.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Hm? A Higashinese wood print?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: It's a landscape...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I've never seen this technique before... the lines are highly expressive.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The colors are bold, almost sacrilegious... but the effect is interesting.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: There's something to be said about this method...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: It's getting late.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: There's been less crying at night lately.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Is the woman who left me that print still here?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I'm busy! Hold on!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I'm coming! Stop knocking!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I believe I said I wasn't going to your 'Relocation Festival'—

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Good evening, Mr. Devlin. We meet again.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Feeling any better?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Your complexion seems brighter. I take it you've been sleeping well.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Why did you come here? I told you—

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Now, it won't do to dig up a lady's shame, would it?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: You said you were busy? Have you been painting?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Just trying out a new technique.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: That's good to hear.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I don't have any questions for you today. Instead, I brought you something. Here.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Flowers?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Yes, I picked them from that hill I mentioned, at around dusk. They still carry the dew on them.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Ordinary flowers, bland colors, unrefined forms... there's no beauty here. They're worthless.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Oh, I didn't bring them for you to admire.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I would like to ask that you paint a still life of them.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: And why would I ever paint something so mundane?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Did you enjoy those Higashinese prints?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I grew up in Higashi. When I went into town with my family, I often saw artists lined up before the great manors, presenting their proudest works to the master of the house.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I had the chance to see many fine paintings, and learned a thing or two about art appreciation.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I picked a few to bring with me when I left Higashi, but admiring art by oneself can be so dull. All the better if they could help someone else in need.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Don't you agree?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Give me the flowers. I'll paint them.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Now what?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Since I'm the one commissioning, perhaps I should lay them out myself.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: It's messy inside...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: And it's cold outside. Would you rather keep chatting here?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...Come in.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Well, you certainly weren't exaggerating when you said it was messy.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I don't see any room for the flowers.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They handed out a lot of useless supplies. I didn't want to waste time cleaning up when it's just a temporary place anyway.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: That won't do. A comfortable environment helps one feel at ease, which is crucial for painting.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Let me help you clean up. For the sake of the painting.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: There's no need for that.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Hm, where should I start?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: What's all this over here?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Don't touch that! I'll do it myself!
20 minutes later.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Just... put that stack of sketch paper over there.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: See, that wasn't so bad, was it? This place is finally fit for habitation.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What a bother... Oh.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The facing of the canvas, the height of the easel, and the position of the flowers...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I caught a glimpse of your room when I went in with you that day. It was very tidy.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I restored it from memory. You didn't take the still life of the flowers hanging on the wall, so I put these where it was.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Do you feel uncomfortable with anything?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: No... it looks just like before the Catastrophe...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: This is what I saw when I turned on the lights after coming back from practice every night... Sometimes I could smell Frau Perry making her soup downstairs.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I never had any, but... it feels warm and fuzzy.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I hope it makes you comfortable.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: But... I never saw these sketches in your room.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I gave them to Frau Perry to dispose of. I didn't expect her to pack them into the suitcase.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Ha. That's how my supplies got ruined. All to save these worthless sketches.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: May I have a look?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Suit yourself. Just practice sketches, barely above scrap paper.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: There are some beautiful landscapes here. Hills, cliffs, meadows... and the setting sun at dusk.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Frau Perry probably thought the same as you. 'Oh, how nice.' So she ruined everything.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Not at all. The depiction of the sunset in these sketches far surpasses the painting that you left at the academy.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Worthless.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...You've seen many Catastrophes, haven't you?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Then you understand that all the sunsets, all the eventides, all the sights of the world are nothing in comparison to one.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I had developed techniques never before seen in Leithanien, combining colors in beautiful and novel ways, perfectly capturing light and shadow in the moment...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: But they rejected it!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: They said it wasn't elegant enough, wasn't detailed enough... those were the pretexts they used to block me from exhibitions.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I thought I wasn't good enough, so I did everything I could to hone my skills. I didn't care about the critics. All I cared about was Herr Leon's approval.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Do you know what he said when I finally showed him the finished sunset I was so proud of?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: He said, 'Your paintings don't move me anymore.'

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Later I understood that it wasn't a matter of technique. I just wasn't meant to make this sort of painting.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: When I saw the prints you gave me yesterday, for a moment I traveled back in time, to when I would fervently try out any new technique. But I came to my senses the moment I put brush to canvas.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I couldn't do it... I couldn't paint such mundane scenery no matter how much I'd changed, because that's not what I live for.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I have the technique, all I need is a more suitable subject, something stunning, to create a true masterpiece. Then they'll understand.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: A sunset? Pah.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The day I picked up the paintbrush, I was destined to travel this path, to dedicate my life to painting the most magnificent sight in the world—

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: A Catastrophe.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I appreciate all that you've done. I'll be leaving once I finish your commission.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Chasing the next Catastrophe?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: If you don't want them anymore, do you mind if I take these sketches?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: If it pleases you. Personally, I'd rather see them all burnt.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I'll take my leave then.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What's that commotion outside?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: That scent... it's familiar...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Frau Perry's soup!

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: You're up, Herr Devlin!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What are you doi—

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: It's the Relocation Festival! Tsukinogi's Post-Catastrophe Mutual Aid Group organized it. It's a day that everyone can relax.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: And your drawings have given the festival such an artistic bent!

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Drawings... my drawings?
He looks up to see threads swaying in the air.
An innumerable number of threads, linking the many sheds together.
From them hang numerous sketches, fluttering in the wind.
His sketches.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: I've told you so many times that your drawings are beautiful, and people should see them, but you would never have any of it.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: I'm not sure how she convinced you, but it's wonderful that everyone gets to see them now.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: No... take them down...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: This is trash! Not art!

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Why? I like your drawings...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: You don't know the first thing about art! If they see them, they'll know just how inept they are—

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Now, I may not know much about art, but I love your drawings from the bottom of my heart.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Besides, art isn't just for certain people.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Wha—

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Seeing your drawings reminds me of home, the one we lost to the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: I still feel sad, of course, but your drawings are so beautiful, they make me think...

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: If we work hard to get our lives back in order, and find the time to travel around once we've settled down, maybe we could see the kind of sights we see in those drawings.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: That's impossible!

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Look around if you don't believe me.

steps.name: Shy Woman
steps.text: Did you see that one of the poplar grove? I wish we could walk through a grove like that, sit down and have a picnic...

steps.name: Kind Man
steps.text: We'll find a place like that when things settle down, I promise.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: That fried egg looks so red, dad. I'm hungry.

steps.name: Calm Man
steps.text: That's not an egg. It's the sun rising in the morning forest mist. It's beautiful.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: The sun! I love the sun.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Everyone loves your drawings.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: It's been awful lately, what with having to abandon our homes and all. Everyone's having a hard time.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Tsukinogi helped a lot, of course, she even fixed my pot. It's all thanks to her that everyone's feeling so much better.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: She planned this festival for us too. I don't know how to thank her.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: She...

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: She also said I should apologize to you.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: I'm so sorry about spilling your paints when I packed your things. I've been thinking about how to make it up to you.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Say, would you like to try some of my soup?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Tsukinogi... have you seen her, Frau Perry?

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: She said that if you asked, I should point you to that little hill to the south of the accommodation site.

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: Oh, hold on, that wasn't all.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Frau Perry
steps.text: She also said she's not there right now. She said you'd know when to find her there, and not to forget your art supplies.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: You know, I think I would like a bowl of soup, please.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Make it a large one.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I see was right about the time.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: It's good to see you, Mr. Devlin.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: As I said, there's a wonderful view here.
The great golden orb sinks towards the horizon in the distance.
It is like the heart of the day, beating futilely to keep the last light alive.
With every pulse, it sends out brilliance beyond reckoning, even as the horizon eats away at it.
But night is inexorable, inevitable.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: It's beautiful, isn't it?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: There was a sunset like that, the day I left Higashi.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Why... Why did you do it?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Well, why didn't you destroy those sketches yourself?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...I'm not in the habit of doing so.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Sit down, Mr. Devlin. Let me tell you a story.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a shrine high in the mountains.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Born to an old and respected family, she was destined at birth to shoulder the clan's future. From a young age, she learned various rituals and dances, and met many important people.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: She hated all that, hated all those frivolous, superficial, impractical things.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: And so, when she grew up, she left home to become a Catastrophe Messenger.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: She used her abilities to help many people escape Catastrophe, but grew estranged from her family.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: One day, a Catastrophe struck near where she had grown up. She managed to evacuate most of the nearby residents, but her family would not leave, and refused to listen to her.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: That was when she realized that she didn't know how to talk to them.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Strange, isn't it? She could convince powerful people in high places, but when it came to her own family, there was nothing she could do except watch the tragedy occur.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: A sad story.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Some people dash towards their dreams, never stopping to look around them.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: The sunset is not a Catastrophe, but neither is one superior to the other. The beauty of the sight lies in whether or not the traveler notices it.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Stop to look around you, once in a while. Don't miss the here and now.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I... I remember now.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I was just a child who loved to draw back then. I would go to the best location in the tavern to sketch the sunset every day at dusk... the feathers dropping from fowlbeasts returning late, the long shadows cast by people in the twilight.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: The workers loved to watch me draw over a drink, laughing that the sunset looked like a fried egg. I said I would draw it even better.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I never threw away those sketches. They were put up on the tavern's walls, and customers would drop a few coins to take home the ones they liked...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: I was happy back then.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Then one day, Herr Leon stood behind me as I drew, and he said...

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: 'My boy, your drawing has moved my heart.'

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: ...So that's what it was.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: But can I still draw like that?

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: With eyes that have gazed too long upon Catastrophes, hands that cannot pick up a paintbrush...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Don't forget that you still owe me a painting.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Let's make it now.

steps.name: Devlin
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: You can paint me dancing.
Her slender form dances in the fading light, whirling with eventide.
Brush touches canvas, capturing the instant in eternity.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Spectacular job, Tsukinogi. This group just set a new record for post-evacuation satisfaction levels, and the results of the psychological assessments are extremely positive.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: This will make subsequent relocation much easier. Hopefully, they'll adjust well to life in the nomadic cities.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Good to hear.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Is this why you always stay behind afterward? To help people escape the shadow of Catastrophe and set their sights on their new lives?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Of course. Life goes on, even after the danger has passed. It's important to move on with the right mindset.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I heard you even helped a painter finish a new work that's earned the praise of Leon, that famous Leithanian artist.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: It's stunned the Leithanian art scene, because Master Leon hasn't reviewed a work of art in over a decade.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Word has it that the painter already has several solo exhibitions lined up.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: He was always a talented artist.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Don't play dumb. What new 'little girl' story did you come up with this time?

spans.text: Don't play dumb. What new 'little girl' story did you come up with

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Have a guess.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: You're asking the impossible... All I know for sure is that you made it sound real.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I have to wonder, though... what made you choose to stay behind after a Catastrophe for the first time?

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: I just hate sadness, that's all.

steps.name: Tsukinogi
steps.text: Anyway, time's a-wasting. There's a mission waiting for us.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Hah, don't worry, you'll have plenty to do.
